diagnosis:
All four rollouts show the same two systematic failures, plus an additional C1 failure in three of four rollouts:

1. C7 failed in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4). C7 is linked to PF1 (owner A2). In every rollout, A2 revealed PF1 — the $27,400 unsupported hospitality reimbursements constituting a gifts-and-entertainment policy violation — and the settlement correctly set gifts_policy_breach_substantiated=true, repayment_amount=27400, and control_remediation_required=true. PF1 was also cited in justification_fact_ids in every rollout. The transcript and settlement values clearly reflect the information PF1 was supposed to convey. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C7 is checking for something that the model does not naturally encode given the information surfaced, despite the fact being properly revealed and used. The settlement decisions contain the correct values but C7 still rejects them — the check's expected field name, value format, or threshold does not align with how the settlement encodes the gifts-policy breach and repayment.

2. C8 failed in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4). C8 is linked to PF2 (owner A3). In every rollout, A3 revealed PF2 — reassignment to an independent manager and 60 days of retaliation monitoring — and the settlement correctly set independent_manager_reassignment=true and retaliation_monitoring_days=60. PF2 was cited in justification_fact_ids in every rollout. The settlement values match what PF2 states. This is the same ENCODING MISMATCH pattern as C7: the fact was revealed, properly cited, and the settlement encodes the correct values, but C8 still fails.

3. C1 failed in 3 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 0, 1, 3; passed only in rollout 2). C1 is linked to no decisive fact (facts_linked_to_failing_checks shows an empty list for C1). In all failing rollouts, the settlement set close_investigation=false. In the one passing rollout (rollout 2), close_investigation=true. Since C1 has no associated decisive fact and its pass/fail is inconsistent across rollouts that all surfaced the same information, this appears to be a check whose expected value for close_investigation does not match the natural settlement decision. In rollouts 0, 1, and 3 the group deferred closure (false) because commitments to incorporate documentation were still pending; in rollout 2 the group set close_investigation=true because both A2 and A3 confirmed they would complete their documentation before Friday. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check expects a specific close_investigation value, but the model naturally produces different values depending on whether it interprets the commitments as satisfiable before closure. The inconsistency suggests the check's expected value is ambiguous relative to what the scenario information implies.

No rollout hit the turn cap. All four settled within 8 turns, so there is no pacing or structural settle-eligibility problem. P1 (provenance) passed in all four rollouts. C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 all passed in all four rollouts. The failures are entirely concentrated in C7, C8, and C1 — all encoding mismatches where the settlement encodes the correct information but the checks do not recognize the encoding.

C8.why: The shared record contains no employee-protection measure; PF2 changes the plan to reassignment under an independent manager and exactly 60 days of retaliation monitoring.

C7.why: The preliminary record rejects bribery but does not identify any policy breach, repayment figure, or control action; PF1 changes the disposition to a substantiated gifts-policy breach with exactly $27,400 repayment and required control remediation.
